title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that quantifies the marginal detection benefit of sandboxed emulation over a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the requested model "gpt-5-mini", we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, execution accounting, artifact-grounded diagnostics, interpretation, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into executable network configurations and operational workflows. Operational trustworthiness for agentic NetOps pipelines depends critically on surrounding deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution that can detect unsafe or incorrect outputs prior to deployment [1], [2]. Although generate→validate→repair is a common mitigation pattern, the marginal value of adding runtime sandboxed emulation atop a strong static validator has not been quantified across a controlled, paired design. We therefore preregistered the confirmatory research question guiding this study: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and system reports argue for workflow-centred mitigations (static validators, formal verification, emulation) to improve NetOps safety and AIOps reliability [1], [2]. Prototype tools and verification transfers show emulation or formal analysis can expose runtime failures missed by static checks in some domains [3]; LLM-for-code and configuration studies document hallucinations and highlight effectiveness gains from external verifiers and repair stages [2], [3]. These works motivate paired, workflow-level measurements that quantify guarded-stage contributions rather than ranking models in isolation. Our study situates itself among this literature by providing an artifact-anchored, preregistered paired estimate of guarded-stage marginal detection in a narrowly scoped experimental regime.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and core design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) prior to any execution. Design: paired-binary under shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each pair a single sampled initial candidate was generated and reused by both baseline and guarded analyses; hence any between-condition discordance can arise only from (i) an emulation observation that the static validator did not flag or (ii) an allowed downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in run accounting. Confirmatory target: Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used in power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). The archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) contains: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reported exactly as produced by the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and archived in analysis/results.json and the analysis CSV artifacts.
sections.discussion: Execution accounting and discordant‑pair attribution. The authoritative execution manifest records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair-stage call). Provider-call audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1, cache_miss_count = 721, cache_hit_count = 0. Because the shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single discordant count (n10 = 1) must be attributable to an emulation observation not covered by the static validator or to the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The unique discordant episode is present as the single entry in execution/raw_results.jsonl where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; independent auditors can locate its pair_id and per-episode validator and emulation traces by searching execution/raw_results.jsonl for that baseline_score/guarded_score pattern and cross-referencing analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json for provider-call accounting. (We do not invent the pair identifier in the text; the archived raw_results entry is the canonical record.)
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection. We interpret the result as arising from a validator ceiling effect combined with curated task design and shared_initial_candidate pairing that constrains discordances to downstream guarded-stage events. We recommend follow-up experiments focused on adversarial and cross-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are discussed in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
